abstract: Oncolytic herpes simplex virus type 1 (oHSV1) is a promising cancer therapy, but tumor cell antiviral responses can restrict viral replication. Strategies for temporally controlled targeting of antiviral factors remain limited. Here, we developed an inducible CRISPR Cas13d platform to modulate host responses during HSV1 infection. We screened 13 pharmacological inhibitors across tumor models to identify pathways associated with restricted infection. Reporter assays identified Cas13d as the preferred effector over Cas13b, while endogenous-target experiments demonstrated Cas13d mediated reductions in target protein abundance. We optimized guide RNA expression using RNA polymerase III promoters, selected p7SK, and established doxycycline-responsive Tet On and Tet Off systems. The platform was incorporated into HSV1 to generate a gRNA library targeting 15 host antiviral genes, together with two non-targeting controls. Doxycycline-dependent reporter readouts demonstrated inducible activity. Evaluation in EMT6, CT26, and 786 O cells revealed guide-dependent differences in fluorescence. These findings establish a programmable framework for investigating virus host interactions during oncolytic HSV infection.

metadata.title: Enhancing the Efficacy of Oncolytic Viruses by Engineering Virus Host Interactions Using CRISPR Cas13d

summary: Inducible CRISPR Cas13d platform engineered into oncolytic HSV1 to knock down host antiviral genes and enhance viral replication in tumor cells.
title: Enhancing the Efficacy of Oncolytic Viruses by Engineering Virus Host Interactions Using CRISPR Cas13d
